strengths: Addresses a meaningful limitation of autoregressive camera-guided generation: early scene choices can conflict with a predefined future camera trajectory. The training-free approach is practically appealing.

Table 1 reports consistently better frame-to-frame and long-range consistency than both baselines across seven trajectory templates, using 40 generations per trajectory. Using the same backbone and adding loop-closing mechanisms to both baselines improves comparability.
The ablations provide useful evidence for combining stochasticity, guidance, and explicit spatial conditioning. Table 3 particularly clearly demonstrates the importance of explicit loop closure.

The manuscript explains the implementation with pseudocode and window diagrams, and candidly documents failures involving external image conditioning, wide-baseline viewpoints, and ambiguous trajectory segments.
weaknesses: The theoretical motivation contains a substantive error. Section 3.2 attributes weak conditioning to using a joint score instead of a conditional score, but their gradients with respect to the target chunk are identical when neighboring chunks are held fixed. Furthermore, updating each chunk using its own conditional score does not generally implement the score of the product in Eq. 3, which also includes derivatives through neighboring factors. The algorithm may work heuristically, but its claimed probabilistic justification is not established.

The Omni Guidance derivation is insufficiently justified. Standard classifier-free guidance does not generally require conditioning values to be independent of model weights in the asserted sense. Moreover, Eq. 8 does not follow merely by merging the two scales in Eq. 7: it replaces two distinct distributions with a jointly unconditioned distribution. This should be presented and evaluated as an additional heuristic, including comparisons that separate camera guidance from neighbor guidance.

The evaluation does not directly establish fidelity to the prescribed camera trajectory, a central claim. There is no camera-pose recovery or motion-adherence metric. Thresholding predicted depth is only a collision proxy, while the consistency metrics can reward oversmoothing, as the paper itself observes. Independent geometric validation or a human evaluation is needed to distinguish faithful navigation from suppressed motion or scene deformation. GVS also ties StochSync on collision avoidance rather than outperforming it.

Generalization evidence is narrow: all quantitative experiments use one 256×256, eight-frame RealEstate10K backbone and seven designed trajectory templates. The 1,080-frame example is qualitative, and spatial windows are specified for the individual trajectory patterns without a demonstrated general construction procedure. Compatibility with any Diffusion-Forcing model is overstated because future conditioning additionally requires suitable bidirectional attention and conditioning support.

The incremental contribution over existing stitching, history guidance, and cyclic window methods is not isolated convincingly. Missing comparisons include straightforward overlapping-window score averaging and matched guidance variants. The baselines also differ in guidance settings and sampling procedures, with no compute-matched analysis, runtime measurements, or memory-scaling results.

Reproducibility and statistical support remain incomplete: collision and field-of-view thresholds are unspecified, uncertainty across generations is not reported, and the guidance strength and window choices receive limited sensitivity analysis. Together with the unresolved derivation and evaluation issues, these omissions leave insufficient evidence for acceptance at a highly selective venue.

strengths: The paper addresses a meaningful limitation of autoregressive camera-guided generation: early scene choices can conflict with a predefined future camera trajectory. A training-free solution using an existing video backbone is practically appealing.

Table 1 provides consistent empirical evidence of improved frame-to-frame and long-range consistency across seven trajectory types, averaged over 40 generations. Using the same backbone and adding loop-closing mechanisms to both baselines makes these comparisons more informative.

The ablations separate stochasticity, Omni Guidance, and explicit loop closure, demonstrating useful quality–consistency tradeoffs. The appendix also candidly documents failures involving external images, wide-baseline viewpoints, and ambiguous trajectory segments.
weaknesses: The mathematical motivation for Omni Guidance is problematic. Section 3.2 attributes weak conditioning to using a joint rather than conditional score, but the target-coordinate gradients of log p(target, neighbors) and log p(target | neighbors) are identical when neighbors are held fixed. Noisy neighbors can weaken available information, but this does not establish the stated joint-versus-conditional distinction. Likewise, the product of conditionals in Eq. 3 does not directly justify the implemented local updates, which omit contributions from other factors containing the target.

The guidance derivation does not adequately distinguish the contribution from existing classifier-free/history guidance. The claim that standard classifier-free guidance requires conditioning independent of model weights is not established, and Eq. 8 does not follow algebraically from Eq. 7 merely by merging guidance scales. The implemented method is plausible as a heuristic, but its theoretical justification and novelty need clearer support.

The evaluation does not directly establish the central claim of camera-trajectory fidelity. MEt3R consistency and inferred-depth collision detection do not measure whether generated camera motion matches the prescribed trajectory. The paper itself shows that oversmoothing can improve consistency scores. Pose-error evaluation, validation of the collision proxy, and perceptual assessment would help distinguish faithful navigation from scene deformation or reduced motion.

Generalization evidence is narrow: experiments use one 256×256 RealEstate10K backbone with an eight-frame context and seven designed trajectory types. Spatial conditioning windows are specified for these trajectories without demonstrating a general selection procedure on arbitrary paths. Compatibility with 'any' Diffusion Forcing model is also overstated because independent noise-level training alone does not ensure access to future frames in a causal architecture.

Comparisons do not sufficiently isolate the proposed advance over simpler stitching alternatives. Baselines comprise autoregressive sampling and an adapted image-oriented StochSync method; direct overlapping-window score averaging and straightforward bidirectional history-guidance variants are missing. There are also no runtime, memory, or compute-matched comparisons supporting the practical advantage of parallel generation.

Important claims exceed the evidence. GVS ties StochSync on measured collisions rather than outperforming it, and aesthetic quality is lower than StochSync on six of seven trajectories. Forty-generation averages lack uncertainty estimates. The 1080-frame demonstration is qualitative, while the Impossible Staircase modifies camera conditioning at the join, so it cannot establish fidelity to one unchanged global trajectory. These limitations, combined with the technical and comparison gaps, leave the submission below the acceptance threshold.

strengths: Addresses a meaningful limitation of autoregressive camera-guided generation: current scene content can conflict with future camera motion. Training-free stitching is a useful approach to this problem.

Results are consistently favorable within the evaluated setting. Across seven trajectories with 40 generations each, GVS achieves better frame-to-frame and long-range consistency than both baselines, with zero detected collisions.
The comparisons use the same backbone, augment autoregression with retrieval, and give StochSync a loop-closing mechanism. These choices help isolate the sampling method's contribution.

Ablations substantiate the roles of stochasticity, Omni Guidance, and cyclic conditioning. For example, explicit loop closing reduces Panorama 1-loop long-range inconsistency from 0.962 to 0.141 with Omni Guidance.

The manuscript provides pseudocode, implementation details, extensive qualitative comparisons, and unusually candid analyses of failures involving external images, wide-baseline viewpoints, and ambiguous staircase segments.

For fixed noisy neighbors, the target-coordinate score of the joint distribution equals that of the corresponding conditional distribution, so their distinction in Section 3.2 does not explain weak conditioning. Furthermore, the local updates are not shown to sample the product distribution in Equation 3, whose score generally includes contributions from multiple factors. Equation 8 is a practical heuristic rather than an established consequence of Equation 7.

The claim of compatibility with any Diffusion-Forcing model is too broad: independent noise-level training alone does not ensure access to future frames, particularly with causal attention. Experiments cover only one 8-frame, 256×256 RealEstate10K backbone, leaving generality across architectures and domains untested.

Evaluation does not directly establish camera-trajectory fidelity or physical collision avoidance. Collision detection relies on inferred depth, while MEt3R can reward oversmoothing, as the paper itself demonstrates. Direct camera-motion accuracy, validated collision measurements, or human evaluation would strengthen the central claims.

The benchmark consists of seven designed trajectories with trajectory-specific spatial windows. General window construction for arbitrary paths is underspecified, uncertainty estimates are absent, and the 1080-frame scaling claim rests on a qualitative example rather than systematic evaluation.

Novelty over existing stitching and history guidance is primarily an effective combination and adaptation. Comparisons against simpler overlapping-window diffusion aggregation and a straightforward bidirectional history-guidance extension would better establish the necessity of the proposed design.

Computational and reproduction details remain incomplete: no runtime, peak-memory, or matched-compute comparisons are reported, and the GVS inference schedule and collision/retrieval thresholds are insufficiently specified. The impossible-staircase demonstration also modifies camera conditioning at the seam, so it should not be interpreted as strict adherence to the original trajectory.

The ablations are substantial, covering guidance, stochasticity, cyclic conditioning, sampling steps, chunk overlap, and three training variants. Runtime and memory measurements also clarify the cost of temporal parallelization.
The paper candidly documents important limitations, including failed external-image conditioning, wide-baseline loop closure, and manually specified spatial windows.

Section 3.2 attributes weak conditioning to using a joint rather than conditional score, but the joint score restricted to the target variables equals the corresponding conditional score when neighboring variables are held fixed. Moreover, the implemented local updates omit cross-factor contributions required by the score of the product distribution in Eq. 3. The sampler may work as a heuristic, but its relationship to the stated distribution is not established.

The novelty of Omni Guidance is insufficiently isolated. Equation 8 closely resembles classifier-free guidance jointly dropping camera and neighboring-frame conditioning, and the paper acknowledges its relationship to fractional history guidance. The claim that model-generated conditioning violates a core classifier-free-guidance assumption is not convincingly justified. Replacing the two guidance terms in Eq. 7 with Eq. 8 also changes the formulation without an ablation establishing the consequences.

Evaluation remains narrow despite the extensive ablations: seven handcrafted trajectories, 40 samples each, and three variants of the same 459M architecture trained on RealEstate10K at 256×256 resolution. These experiments do not establish compatibility with arbitrary Diffusion-Forcing models, particularly models whose attention structure prevents future conditioning. Manually designed spatial windows further limit evidence of generalization to unseen trajectories.

The metrics do not adequately establish trajectory fidelity or genuinely collision-free navigation. Estimated-depth thresholding can miss violations of the intended motion, and consistency metrics can benefit from oversmoothing, as the paper itself demonstrates. There is no direct camera-pose accuracy evaluation or independent validation of the collision detector. Aesthetic quality is also consistently below StochSync in Table 1, making the consistency–quality tradeoff important.

The comparison omits straightforward overlapping-window score-fusion alternatives, such as a video adaptation of MultiDiffusion, which would help isolate the value of discarding conditioning outputs and using the proposed stitching schedule. Baseline guidance and sampling settings are not systematically tuned, and uncertainty estimates are absent.

The strongest demonstrations have limited practical scope: external image conditioning fails, wide-baseline loop closure fails, and the impossible-staircase example modifies camera conditioning at the seam. These acknowledged constraints substantially narrow the broader claims about faithful, globally coherent camera-guided generation.

Section 3.2 attributes weak conditioning to using a joint rather than conditional score, but for fixed neighboring noisy variables, the target-coordinate score of their joint distribution equals the corresponding conditional score. Moreover, independently assembling local conditional scores does not generally yield the score of the product distribution in Eq. 3, which also requires contributions from neighboring factors. The sampler may work empirically, but its stated distributional interpretation is not established.

Omni Guidance is insufficiently distinguished from existing guidance. The implemented Eq. 8 closely resembles joint camera and history classifier-free guidance extended to two-sided noisy context, as the paper itself acknowledges. Eq. 8 does not generally follow by simply merging the two distinct guidance terms in Eq. 7. Comparisons against separately weighted camera and neighbor guidance, and ordinary guidance within the same stitching sampler, would clarify the contribution.

The evaluation does not directly establish camera-trajectory fidelity or physically meaningful collision avoidance. Predicted-depth thresholding and MEt3R consistency can reward oversmoothing, reduced motion, or altered geometry; the paper itself documents this ambiguity. There is no explicit camera-pose tracking metric, independent geometric validation, or human evaluation to distinguish faithful navigation from visually plausible scene deformation.

Spatial conditioning windows are manually specified per trajectory. Consequently, the experiments do not demonstrate an automatic method for arbitrary paths or substantiate compatibility with any Diffusion Forcing model, especially architectures that cannot attend to future frames.

Baseline coverage is limited to history-guided autoregression and an adapted image-stitching method. Direct comparisons with simpler overlapping-window score fusion or averaging would help establish whether the proposed stitching design is necessary. The current comparisons leave the incremental benefit over straightforward combinations of existing techniques uncertain.

The reported means lack uncertainty estimates, and some gains are small, such as staircase-circuit F2FC of 0.129 versus 0.132 for autoregression. Quality tradeoffs are also material: GVS has lower aesthetic quality than StochSync on six of seven trajectories. The 1080-frame demonstration is qualitative, while the impossible-staircase example explicitly modifies camera conditioning at the seam, limiting its value as evidence of fidelity to the original trajectory.

strengths: The paper addresses a meaningful limitation of autoregressive camera-guided generation: predefined future camera motion can conflict with an already generated scene. A training-free sampler that jointly reconciles video segments is a useful contribution.

Results show consistent improvements on the seven tested trajectories. In Table 1, GVS achieves better frame-to-frame and long-range consistency than both baselines wherever these metrics apply, and eliminates detected collisions relative to autoregressive sampling.

The experimental analysis is substantial within the chosen setting: 40 generations per trajectory, ablations of guidance, stochasticity, loop closure, sampling steps, and chunking, plus experiments with three training variants of the backbone.

The appendix provides useful implementation and computational details, including a fair throughput comparison with batched autoregressive sampling. The discussion candidly documents failures in external-image conditioning, wide-baseline loop closure, and global information propagation.
weaknesses: The probabilistic justification needs correction. Section 3.2 attributes weak consistency to using a joint rather than conditional score, but for fixed neighboring variables, the target-variable gradients of log p(target, neighbors) and log p(target | neighbors) are identical. Moreover, the local updates are not shown to sample the product-of-conditionals distribution in Eq. 3, and Eq. 8 is a heuristic replacement rather than an algebraic simplification of Eq. 7. The empirical method may remain useful, but the proposed explanation does not establish its correctness.

Evaluation does not directly establish fidelity to the commanded camera trajectory, a central claim. MEt3R measures visual consistency, and estimated-depth thresholding is only a proxy for collisions; neither verifies camera translation and rotation. The documented wide-baseline failure demonstrates that visually consistent outputs can follow incorrect viewpoints. Pose-error measurements and validation of the collision proxy are needed.

Generalization remains limited. All three backbones share the same 459M architecture, eight-frame context, resolution, and RealEstate10K training data. Loop-closing windows are manually specified for each trajectory, with no quantitative evaluation on diverse held-out paths. Compatibility with 'any' Diffusion-Forcing model is also overstated: independent per-frame noise training does not itself guarantee access to future tokens under causal attention.

Comparisons do not sufficiently isolate the contribution beyond existing stitching and guidance techniques. The principal stitching baseline is an adaptation of StochSync from image generation; comparisons with simpler overlapping-window score fusion or alternative window schedules would strengthen the novelty claim. Omni Guidance closely extends existing history guidance, making these controlled comparisons especially important.

Practical and statistical evidence remains incomplete. Image conditioning fails, restricting use for scene-specific cinematography, and the impossible-staircase example modifies camera conditioning at the seam. Results have no uncertainty estimates or human temporal-quality assessment, despite acknowledged smoothing-related metric confounds. These limitations leave the broader applicability and perceptual benefit less established than the headline claims suggest.
